title: Splitwise: Efficient generative LLM inference using phase splitting
technique: split prompt and token phases onto separate machine pools (homogeneous/heterogeneous GPUs, power-capped), KV-cache transfer over InfiniBand, mixed pool; cluster provisioning search for throughput/cost/power

optimized_metrics.evidence: Using Splitwise, we design homogeneous and heterogeneous LLM inference clusters optimized for throughput, cost, and power.

headline_claim.text: Compared to current designs, Splitwise clusters achieve up to 1.4x higher throughput at 20% lower cost. Alternatively, they can deliver 2.35x more throughput under the same power and cost budgets.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 17-19 cluster designs (max RPS meeting SLOs)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: End-to-end (E2E) latency: Total query time that the user sees
Time to first token (TTFT): How quickly user sees initial response
metric_definitions.notes: no explicit statement on queueing, but cluster simulation reports per-request TTFT under load (incl. queues)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We add another latency metric: time between tokens (TBT), to track the online streaming throughput of the tokens as they are generated serially.  [Table II:] Time between tokens (TBT): Average token streaming latency
metric_definitions.notes: Table II says 'Average token streaming latency' but SLOs are applied to P50/P90/P99 of TBT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For the prompt phase, we define the throughput as the number of prompt input tokens that are processed per second.
metric_definitions.notes: phase-wise: prompt phase counts input tokens, token phase counts generated tokens
cluster throughput = max RPS satisfying all nine SLOs

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Table VI: SLO expressed as slowdown compared to a request running on DGX-A100 under no contention. [P50/P90/P99] TTFT 2x/3x/6x; TBT 1.25x/1.5x/5x; E2E 1.25x/1.5x/5x
metric_definitions.notes: 9 SLOs, all must be met; relative-slowdown SLOs, not absolute

slo_spec: Table VI: slowdown vs a contention-free request on DGX-A100; P50/P90/P99 for TTFT = 2x/3x/6x, TBT = 1.25x/1.5x/5x, E2E = 1.25x/1.5x/5x; all nine must hold; TTFT slightly looser since smaller impact on E2E
load_regime: trace replay shapes with Poisson arrival-rate sweep (requests/s) for cluster sizing; iso-power, iso-cost, iso-throughput comparisons
tradeoff_acknowledged: KV-cache transfer overhead (<7% of prompt time; up to 3% of E2E in serialized case); mixed continuous batching hurts TBT; prompt phase sensitive to power cap while token phase is not; lower cost designs (A100 token machines) trade some latency
hardware: DGX-A100 and DGX-H100 (characterization on H100; cluster simulator with A100/H100 mixes)
workloads: Microsoft production traces: coding and conversation (Azure); Poisson arrivals
extractor_notes: Cluster results come from a simulator validated against hardware. Multiple objectives depending on design question (iso-power throughput-optimized, iso-throughput cost/power-optimized); P99 constraints are expressed as slowdown ratios. Characterization throughput (tokens/s per phase) differs from cluster throughput (RPS).

tail_audit.metrics: TTFT, TBT, E2E @ P50/P90/P99 (nine SLOs, all must hold)
